# Models

Sections

## Choosing a model for agents. Tool and function calling quality, instruction following, context length, speed, and cost per task.

## Context windows and token economics. Pricing, caching, and how long-running agents use up tokens.

## Reasoning modes and effort settings. When thinking models are worth the extra time and cost.

## Access and hosting. Direct APIs, model routers like OpenRouter, cloud platforms like Bedrock, Vertex and Azure, and running models locally.

## Running models locally. Quantization, file formats like GGUF and MLX, and hardware sizing, which builds on what we covered about the 5090 and DGX Spark.

## Licensing. The difference between open weights and fully open models like Olmo, plus Apache-style licenses versus custom ones like Llama's.

## Fine-tuning and distillation. LoRA and when adapting a model beats prompting it.

## Model lifecycle. Versioning, deprecations, and pinning a model version so an agent behaves the same over time.


## Types of AI Models

- General-purpose and code-specialized large language models
- Multimodal models
- Image-generation models, including text-to-image and image-to-image systems
- Decision or “System One” models, including calibrated-decision approaches

## AI Model Types

- Large Language Models (LLM)
  - General-purpose language models
    - Claude (Anthropic)
    - GPT (OpenAI)
    - Gemini (Google DeepMind)
    - Grok (xAI)
    - Open-weight leaders: Kimi (Moonshot AI), DeepSeek, Qwen (Alibaba), MiMo (Xiaomi), GLM (Zhipu AI / Z.AI)
  - Code-specialized models
    - Codex models (OpenAI)
    - Qwen3-Coder (Alibaba)
    - Codestral / Devstral (Mistral AI)
- Image Generation Models
  - Text-to-Image
    - [FLUX](https://blackforestlabs.ai/)
    - [GPT Image](https://openai.com/) (successor to DALL-E)
    - [Grok Imagine](https://grok.com/supergrok/imagine)
    - [Ideogram](https://ideogram.ai/)
    - [Imagen](https://deepmind.google/models/imagen/)
    - [Midjourney](https://www.midjourney.com/home)
    - [Seedream](https://www.bytedance.com/)
    - [Stable Diffusion](https://stablediffusionweb.com/)
  - Image-to-Image
    - [FLUX Kontext](https://blackforestlabs.ai/), Gemini image editing (Google), GPT Image editing (OpenAI)
- Video Generation Models
  - [Grok Imagine](https://grok.com/supergrok/imagine)
  - [Kling](https://klingai.com/)
  - [Runway Gen](https://runwayml.com/)
  - Sora (OpenAI)

- Embedding Models
  - [Cohere Embed](https://cohere.com/)
  - Gemini embeddings (Google)
  - [Voyage](https://www.voyageai.com/)
- Multimodal Models (Text, Image, Audio, Video)
  - Claude (Anthropic)
  - Gemini (Google DeepMind)
  - GPT (OpenAI)
  - Grok (xAI)
  - Kimi (Moonshot AI)
  - Llama / Muse (Meta)
  - Qwen (Alibaba)



## Model families and access

The landscape includes models from Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT), Google
DeepMind (Gemini and Gemma), DeepSeek, Alibaba (Qwen), Meta (Llama and Muse),
xAI (Grok), Moonshot (Kimi), Mistral, and Zhipu (GLM). Open-weight and
closed models differ in how they can be inspected, hosted, adapted, and
accessed.

## Evaluation and training data

Benchmarks help compare models, but scores need context. Some benchmarks, such
as MMLU and GSM8K, are nearing saturation; others, including SWE-bench
variants, LiveBench, LMArena, GAIA, and BenchLM, provide different signals.
Training data sources such as Common Crawl and FineWeb also shape model
capabilities.

## Abliteration

Refusal-removal techniques and fine-tunes, including Heretic and Ajax, can
change how a model responds. Consider their impact on behavior and agent
autonomy when selecting a model.

## Benchmarks

| Benchmark                                                                                                                         | Status in 2026                                | Strengths                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Weaknesses                                                                                                                                                                                               | Still useful?                                                                                                                                                      |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **MMLU**                                                                                                                          | Saturated                                     | Historical reference for broad knowledge                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Frontier models cluster ~90%+; little differentiation; contamination risk                                                                                                                                | Mostly no (use MMLU-Pro if needed)                                                                                                                                 |
| **GSM8K**                                                                                                                         | Saturated                                     | Simple math word problems                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Top models near ceiling (~95%+); many invalid questions noted                                                                                                                                            | No for frontier comparison                                                                                                                                         |
| **GPQA** (Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark; esp. Diamond)                                                                | Near-saturating                               | Challenging multiple-choice benchmark evaluating advanced scientific reasoning and deep domain understanding in large language models                                                                                                                                                       | Leaders pushing 90%+; small set → noise                                                                                                                                                                  | Still decent for science reasoning, but headroom shrinking                                                                                                         |
| **SWE-bench** (Verified/Pro variants)                                                                                             | Contested / partially saturating              | Real GitHub issue resolution; strong signal for coding agents                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Contamination concerns; scores climbing into high 70s–90s on easier versions                                                                                                                             | Yes for coding/agentic work (prefer newer/harder variants like Pro)                                                                                                |
| **GAIA**                                                                                                                          | Active but contested                          | Multi-step agentic tasks (browsing, tools, files) that are easy for humans                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Large score gaps depending on scaffolding/tools; some saturation reports                                                                                                                                 | Yes for assistant/agent evaluation                                                                                                                                 |
| [**LiveBench**](https://livebench.ai/#/)                                                                                          | Highly regarded                               | Monthly-refreshed questions from recent sources; objective ground-truth scoring; covers reasoning, coding, math, data analysis, language, instruction following                                                                                                                             | Not human preference; not pure agentic long-horizon                                                                                                                                                      | **One of the strongest current objective capability benchmarks**                                                                                                   |
| [**LMArena**](https://lmarena.ai/) (Chatbot/Arena)                                                                                | Highly regarded                               | Large-scale blind human preference (Elo-style); real user prompts                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Style/verbosity bias; overlapping confidence intervals; not verifiable correctness                                                                                                                       | **Best for “which model feels best in open-ended use”**                                                                                                            |
| [**BenchLM**](https://benchlm.ai/)                                                                                                | Aggregator                                    | Combines many sources into overall indices                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Depends on underlying benchmarks; not a primary eval itself                                                                                                                                              | Useful meta-view, not a standalone benchmark                                                                                                                       |
| **Mensa Norway IQ Test**                                                                                                          | Niche                                         | Attempts IQ-style scoring                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Narrow, not standard in frontier AI evaluation                                                                                                                                                           | Rarely used for serious model comparison                                                                                                                           |
| **WebDev Arena**                                                                                                                  | Specialized                                   | Web development tasks                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Narrow domain                                                                                                                                                                                            | Useful only if you care specifically about web-dev agents                                                                                                          |
| [**Humanity's Last Exam**](https://lastexam.ai/) (HLE)                                                                            | Active frontier benchmark                     | Expert-authored (≈1,000 contributors) multi-modal closed-ended questions (2,500 total) at the frontier of human knowledge across 100+ subjects; designed to resist search/contamination; objective grading; HLE-Diamond & Rolling variants for continued headroom                           | Score variance across full set / text-only / Diamond / with-tools; some answer-key disputes (esp. chem/bio); calibration remains poor                                                                    | **Yes — currently one of the strongest non-saturated academic/knowledge + reasoning benchmarks**                                                                   |
| [**WorkBuddy Bench**](https://github.com/Tencent/workbuddy-bench) (Tencent)                                                       | Active / Research Preview (v1.2, Oct 2026)    | Multi-domain coding-agent eval (Code 80 / Web 70 / Office 50 / Security 60 tasks) reverse-engineered from real work; contamination-resistant prompts; dual harnesses (CodeBuddy Code + Claude Code); fully open (tasks, Docker images, tests, solutions); reports efficiency (tokens/turns) | No suite-wide average (subset scores incomparable); harness effects are large; still early / Research Preview; heavier compute than pure unit-test benchmarks                                            | **Yes — one of the strongest current multi-domain agentic coding benchmarks**, especially for real-world role-played work beyond pure SWE-bench-style issue fixing |
| [**Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5**](https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/artificial-analysis-intelligence-index) | Active frontier composite (launched Oct 2026) | Independent composite of 9 hard evaluations (Knowledge Work / Coding / Science / General at 25% each); 60% private or held-out data to resist contamination; strong agentic emphasis (FrontierCode 2.0, Terminal-Bench-Science, AA-Briefcase); no single model dominates all components     | Version scores not comparable to prior AA indices; heavy reliance on private tests reduces external auditability; mainly English text-only; effort settings and harness can shift rankings significantly | **Yes — currently one of the most-watched single-number frontier rankings for overall capability, especially agentic/knowledge-work + coding**                     |
| [**Terminal-Bench**](https://www.tbench.ai/)                                                                                      | Active (2.x line)                             | Real command-line tasks in sandboxed containers (builds, debugging, sysadmin, data work); tests end-to-end agent behavior, not just code output; open tasks and harness; widely cited by labs and composite indices                                                                         | Results depend heavily on the agent harness; tasks vary in difficulty and flakiness; long-running and compute-heavy                                                                                      | **Yes — a core benchmark for terminal and coding agents**                                                                                                          |
| [**τ-bench / τ²-bench**](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench) (Sierra)                                                  | Active                                        | Tool-using agents in multi-turn conversations with a simulated user under domain policies (retail, airline, telecom); pass^k metric measures consistency across repeated runs                                                                                                               | Simulated-user behavior adds noise; narrow customer-service domains; some task and label errors reported                                                                                                 | **Yes — one of the best tests of policy-following, reliability, and tool use in conversation**                                                                     |
| [**OSWorld**](https://os-world.github.io/) (incl. OSWorld-Verified)                                                               | Active, scores rising fast                    | Agents operate real desktop operating systems and apps (Ubuntu, Windows, macOS) through screenshots and mouse/keyboard; execution-based checking; human baseline about 72%                                                                                                                  | Slow and costly to run; environment setup and flaky tasks; scores sensitive to screenshot resolution and step limits                                                                                     | **Yes — the standard benchmark for computer-use agents**                                                                                                           |
| [**BrowseComp**](https://openai.com/index/browsecomp/) (OpenAI)                                                                   | Active, climbing                              | 1,266 hard-to-find but easy-to-verify questions that need persistent, creative web browsing; short answers allow objective grading                                                                                                                                                          | Answers can leak onto the web over time; measures finding facts, not synthesis or report quality; English-centric (BrowseComp-ZH covers Chinese)                                                         | **Yes — the go-to benchmark for deep-research and web-browsing agents**                                                                                            |
| [**MCP-Universe**](https://mcp-universe.github.io/) (Salesforce) and other MCP benchmarks (MCP-Bench, MCPMark)                    | Emerging                                      | Agents use real Model Context Protocol servers (GitHub, maps, finance, browser, etc.) on multi-step tasks; execution-based checking; directly mirrors how modern agents connect to tools                                                                                                    | Young and fragmented, with no single standard; depends on live third-party services that change; long-context and unfamiliar-tool challenges skew results                                                | **Yes, if you build MCP-based agents** — watch for consolidation                                                                                                   |
| [**METR Time Horizons**](https://metr.org/)                                                                                       | Active, widely cited                          | Measures the length of tasks (in human expert time) an agent completes with 50% reliability; tracks the trend over time (roughly doubling every ~7 months); grounded in software and research tasks                                                                                         | Wide confidence intervals; task suite skews toward software and ML; 50% reliability is far below production needs; not a leaderboard of everyday performance                                             | **Yes — the best single measure of how autonomous agents are becoming**                                                                                            |
| [**ARC-AGI**](https://arcprize.org/) (ARC-AGI-2 / ARC-AGI-3)                                                                      | Active, far from saturated on newer versions  | Novel visual grid puzzles that test abstraction and skill acquisition on unseen problems; easy for humans, hard for models; cost-per-task reported alongside scores; ARC-AGI-3 adds interactive game-like environments                                                                      | Narrow puzzle domain; results swing with test-time compute budgets; limited direct transfer to agentic work                                                                                              | **Yes — the leading test of genuine novel reasoning rather than memorization**                                                                                     |
| [**Aider Polyglot**](https://aider.chat/docs/leaderboards/)                                                                       | Near-saturating at the top                    | 225 hard Exercism exercises across C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, and Rust; tests the model's ability to make correct edits in a real coding workflow; reports cost and edit-format compliance                                                                                          | Exercise-style problems, not real repositories; public exercises raise contamination risk; top models cluster high                                                                                       | Somewhat — useful for comparing code-editing reliability and cost; less so at the frontier                                                                   |

## Model Training Data

### Pretraining Corpora
(Order by Name ↑)

- [C4 (Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/c4) -- cleaned Common Crawl text used to train T5 and many later models.
- [Common Crawl](https://commoncrawl.org/) -- the raw open web crawl underlying most pretraining datasets.
- [Dolma](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/dolma) (Ai2) -- fully open pretraining corpus behind the Olmo models.
- [FineWeb](https://huggingface.co/spaces/HuggingFaceFW/blogpost-fineweb-v1) -- curated, deduplicated Common Crawl dataset.
- [FineWeb-Edu](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu) -- educational-quality subset of FineWeb.
- [FineWeb 2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-2) -- multilingual extension of FineWeb.
- [LAION / Re-LAION-5B](https://laion.ai/) -- large image-text pair dataset used to train image models such as Stable Diffusion.
- [RedPajama](https://www.together.ai/blog/redpajama-data-v2) (Together AI) -- open reproduction of the LLaMA training data mix.
- [The Pile](https://pile.eleuther.ai/) (EleutherAI) -- diverse 800 GB English text corpus from 22 sources.
- [The Stack v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/bigcode/the-stack-v2) (BigCode) -- large permissively licensed source-code dataset; key for code and agentic models.

### Post-Training and Agent Datasets
(Order by Name ↑)

- [Dolci](https://huggingface.co/collections/allenai/olmo-hybrid) (Ai2) -- supervised fine-tuning data for Olmo Think and Instruct models, including tool-use sets.
- [SWE-Gym](https://github.com/SWE-Gym/SWE-Gym) -- environment and agent trajectories for training software-engineering agents on real GitHub tasks.
- [SWE-smith](https://github.com/SWE-bench/SWE-smith) -- toolkit and dataset for generating software-engineering tasks and coding-agent trajectories at scale.
- [Tulu 3](https://huggingface.co/collections/allenai/tulu-3-datasets) (Ai2) -- open instruction-tuning and preference data, with recipes.
